the disruption of the cell membranes by carbon nanotubes can occur in electrostatic repulsion conditions.
electrostatic interactions between MWCNTs and cell membranes are not sufficient to explain the disruption of cell membranes, and that MWCNT surface properties are critical factors.

(1) electrostatically repulsing conditions do not protect the membranes from MWCNTs, (2) the defect degree of the MWCNTs correlates with their adhesion amounts on the membrane, and (3) the defect sites on the MWCNT surfaces are active binding sites whether they are oxygenated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of charge and surface defect of multi-walled CNTs (MWCNT) on the disruption of lipid bilayers.
the effects of electrostatic interactions and the surface defects of MWCNT on the disruption of cell membranes.

the effects of charge and surface properties of multi-walled nanotubes (MWNTs) on their interaction with cell membranes, which is important for the understanding of the toxicity of nanomaterials and the development of safe applications.

the MWCNT surface properties, such as charge, defects, and the degree of defects, have significant influences on the disruption of membranes.
the electrostatic interactions between MWCNTs and membranes play an important role in the membrane disruption, while MWCNT defects also play an important role by providing binding sites.
electrostatic forces play a key role in the interaction of MWCNT and cell membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
electrostatic interaction is not the sole mechanism of MWCNT-cell membrane interactions, and MWCN defects are active binding sites.
the electrostatic forces and the surface defects of MWCNT were the main factors affecting MWCNT-membnane interactions.
the MWCNTs with high defect degree can disrupt the model cell membranes through electrostatic interaction or phospholipid extration, depending on the charge of MWCNT surface and model membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the disruption of cell membranes by carbon nanotubes is not solely due to electrostatic forces, and that the defects on the surface of the carbon nanotubes play a significant role.
MWCNTs can disrupt model cell membranes, and this is due to electrostatic and non-electrostatic interactions between the MWCNTs and the cell membranes.
electrostatic interactions are not the only factor that determines the cytotoxicity of MWCNT.
